headline: Highest risk is data leakage from plano’s broad egress and file/API surfaces; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by the pair’s lack of shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while profile B has an OpenAI-compatible API and file config surface. There is no documented shared channel or direct ingestion path between them, so only an unusual manual copy-paste or external bridge could create injection risk.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-derived text into B prompts or config files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the pair, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted text from A into B prompts.
Add a review step before B consumes any A-generated content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any shared text channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B touches logs, traces, metrics, and has broad network egress plus an OpenAI-compatible API. If A and B are co-located on a shared workspace or B receives A-derived artifacts, B can transmit them off-host by default. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF A-derived files are placed in B's config or input path, B can exfiltrate them via network egress.
IF both agents share a workspace, B may read and transmit artifacts created for A.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in B's workspace.
Restrict B's outbound network destinations.
Separate A and B storage directories.
Review B logs for accidental payload capture.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or runtime surfaces; B can call APIs and read config.yaml but cannot spawn subprocesses or run browsers. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared lock domain documented, direct capability conflict is limited and likely requires extra orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF B is configured to mutate shared API state while A is extended with write surfaces, contention becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-owner.
Disable shared write mounts.
Serialize any shared API mutations.
Document ownership of config.yaml and related files.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static repository listing and does not generate operational facts, while B is a travel-planning gateway with API routing. There is no documented pipeline where B treats A’s output as authoritative, so cascading error would require an external workflow that is not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF an operator uses A as a source of policy or facts for B, B may propagate errors.
IF B is configured to auto-act on upstream text without verification, downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on upstream text.
Do not use A as an authoritative facts source.
Add validation checks on B inputs.
Log provenance for any imported content.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source repository with no touched data classes, while B explicitly handles logs, traces, and metrics and has broad egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operational logging/retention gaps rather than a proven breach path.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B's logs or traces, retention and residency controls become relevant.
IF B is deployed under a jurisdictional policy stricter than its default logging behavior, a mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through B.
Review B retention settings.
Minimize log verbosity.
Confirm deployment region and data handling policy.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
